UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores additional, application-specific user information beyond authentication details handled by an external system like Firebase Auth.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity, matching the external authentication system's user ID (e.g., Firebase UID).

email.description: The user's email address, often used for display purposes and unique identification within the application.

displayName.description: The user's preferred display name, used for personalization in the UI.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was last updated.

Outbreak.title: Outbreak
Outbreak.description: Represents a specific disease outbreak cluster identified globally, used for heatmap visualization and reporting.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Outbreak entity.

diseaseName.description: The common name of the disease associated with this outbreak (e.g., 'COVID-19', 'Ebola').

latitude.description: The geographical latitude coordinate of the outbreak's primary location.

longitude.description: The geographical longitude coordinate of the outbreak's primary location.

countryCode.description: The ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code where the outbreak is primarily located.

regionName.description: A broader regional or administrative name where the outbreak is located (e.g., 'Europe', 'North America').

intensityLevel.description: A numerical value representing the intensity or severity of the outbreak, used to determine the shade on the heatmap overlay.

status.description: The current status of the outbreak (e.g., 'Active', 'Contained', 'Resolved').

startDate.description: The date and time when the outbreak was first identified or officially started.

lastUpdateDate.description: The date and time when the data for this outbreak was last updated.

sourceUrl.description: A URL pointing to the original data source or official report for this outbreak information.

affectedCount.description: The estimated number of individuals affected by this outbreak.

fatalityCount.description: The estimated number of fatalities directly attributed to this outbreak.

category.description: The epidemiological category or type of the disease (e.g., 'Viral', 'Bacterial', 'Zoonotic').

aiProcessedInsights.description: Textual insights or a summary generated by the Outbreak Data Processor (GenAI) tool regarding this specific outbreak.

OutbreakReport.title: OutbreakReport
OutbreakReport.description: Represents a generated analytical report summarizing information about one or more disease outbreaks, accessible in the reports section.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OutbreakReport entity.

title.description: The title of the outbreak report.

generatedDate.description: The date and time when this report was generated.

reportContent.description: The main content or summary of the report. This could be plain text, markdown, or a URI to a larger document.

outbreakIds.description: An array of IDs referencing the Outbreak entities included or discussed within this report. (Relationship: Outbreak N:N OutbreakReport)

userId.description: Optional reference to the UserProfile who generated or saved this report. If null, the report is system-generated or globally available to authenticated users. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N OutbreakReport)

definition.description: Stores individual user profile data. Access is restricted to the authenticated user whose `uid` matches the `userId` path parameter. The document's 'id' field must match 'userId'.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Contains global disease outbreak data for heatmap visualization. This data is read-only and accessible to all authenticated users (including anonymous guests).

params.name: outbreakId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific disease outbreak.

definition.description: Stores system-generated outbreak reports. This data is read-only and accessible to all authenticated users (including anonymous guests). The 'userId' field in the document schema is ignored for these reports, as they are system-owned.

params.name: reportId
params.description: The unique identifier for a system-generated outbreak report.

definition.description: Stores outbreak reports generated by a specific user. Access (read/write) is restricted to the user whose `uid` matches the `userId` path parameter. Includes denormalized 'userId' field for authorization independence, matching the path parameter.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this report, matching Firebase Authentication UID.

params.name: reportId
params.description: The unique identifier for a user-generated outbreak report.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and QAPs (Queryable Authorization Patterns) through strategic use of structural segregation and denormalization. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **User Profiles (`/userProfiles/{userId}`):** User profiles are stored in a top-level collection, with the document ID (`{userId}`) directly matching the Firebase Authentication UID (`request.auth.uid`). This inherently makes authorization independent, as access can be determined solely by comparing the requested path's `userId` with `request.auth.uid`, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to other documents.
2.  **User-Specific Outbreak Reports (`/userProfiles/{userId}/outbreakReports/{reportId}`):** By nesting user-generated reports under the user's profile, the `userId` from the path (`{userId}`) directly dictates ownership. For robustness and explicit intent, the `OutbreakReport` document itself will include a `userId` field that matches the parent `userId`. This denormalization ensures that rules can be evaluated atomically at the document level without requiring cross-document lookups (`get()`), thus achieving full authorization independence.
3.  **Global Data (`/outbreaks/{outbreakId}` and `/systemOutbreakReports/{reportId}`):** For data that is public to all authenticated users, authorization is independent of specific document fields or user roles. Access is granted simply by checking `request.auth != null`, making rules straightforward and atomic.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
1.  **Structural Segregation for Homogeneous Security:**
    *   `Outbreaks` data (`/outbreaks/{outbreakId}`) is placed in a dedicated collection where all documents share the same security posture (read-only for all authenticated users). The rule `allow read: if request.auth != null;` is QAP compliant because any `list` operation on this collection will only return documents that are permissible under this rule.
    *   `System Outbreak Reports` (`/systemOutbreakReports/{reportId}`) are similarly segregated. All documents in this collection are readable by any authenticated user. The rule `allow read: if request.auth != null;` ensures QAP compliance for `list` queries, as all documents match the security requirement.
    *   `User Profiles` (`/userProfiles/{userId}`) and `User-Specific Outbreak Reports` (`/userProfiles/{userId}/outbreakReports/{reportId}`) are structured using path-based ownership. For example, a user can only query or list documents within `/userProfiles/{request.auth.uid}/outbreakReports`. The security rules will directly compare `request.auth.uid` to the `{userId}` wildcard in the path, ensuring that `list` operations are implicitly filtered by the security context of the path itself, adhering to QAPs.

This design leverages structural clarity to simplify security rules, making them easier to write, debug, and reason about, while strictly adhering to the core design principles.
